headline: Graft charges over Sabah mining licences; the 1999 law to overhaul that system is still not in force
context: Shamsul Iskandar, a former senior political secretary to the Prime Minister, pleaded not guilty in December 2025 to five corruption charges over alleged gratification linked to Sabah mineral-licence approvals. The Mineral Enactment 1999, meant to overhaul that licensing, has never been brought into force.

cards.big: A former senior political secretary to the Prime Minister faces five graft charges over alleged payments linked to Sabah mineral-licence approvals. The law to overhaul that licensing passed in 1999 and was never switched on.
cards.sub: Shamsul Iskandar pleaded not guilty in December 2025 to charges under MACC Act section 17(a), with the alleged gratification tied to businessman Albert Tei. The Mineral Enactment 1999 has sat unenforced for 27 years.

cards.big: Shamsul Iskandar pleaded not guilty in December 2025 to five counts under MACC Act section 17(a). The case has not gone to trial.
cards.sub: Section 17(a) is punishable under section 24(1): up to 20 years' jail and a fine of at least five times the gratification. The alleged items span cash, furniture, electrical goods and rent. In April 2026 a High Court judge rejected an application to move the case up from the Sessions Court; an appeal followed.

cards.big: Sabah still licenses mining under a 1960 ordinance. The Director grants prospecting licences with the Minister's approval; mining leases need the State Cabinet.
cards.sub: The Mineral Enactment 1999, passed by the state assembly to create a new mineral-tenement regime, would repeal the 1960 ordinance once in force. The Sabah Attorney-General's Chambers still lists it as not yet in force.

cards.big: The alleged giver, businessman Albert Tei, was charged in June 2025 in a separate RM350,000 mineral-licence case alongside two Sabah assemblymen.
cards.sub: Media reports link Tei to video recordings that drew wider attention to the Sabah licensing allegations from late 2024. He is now both an accused man and, in Shamsul's case, the alleged giver.

cards.big: A courtroom can weigh what a person did. It cannot enact the law Sabah wrote in 1999 to replace the framework these licences run on.
Sabah passed a new rulebook in 1999, then kept running the 1960 one because the new one's start date was never appointed.
cards.sub: The replacement law exists on paper. Until a minister gazettes its commencement, the old ordinance still governs.

cards.big: The charges will be settled in court. The 1999 law that would overhaul Sabah's mineral licensing will not be, and until a minister gazettes it, the 1960 ordinance still governs.
